name: orbit_auto_task_add
description: Create a recurring auto-task definition. The generic scheduler mints a task from its template on each due slot.

name.description: Unique definition name (lowercase alphanumeric, `-`/`_`, starts alphanumeric). Required.

description.description: Human description of the recurring chore.

schedule.description: Schedule object: exactly one of `{ cron: string }` (5-field cron) `{ every_minutes: number }`, `{ deliveries_landed: { branch, threshold, max_wait_minutes, coverage, owner_machine?, max_items?, retries? } }` (coverage: landed_code_review_v1; owner_machine defaults to this workspace's registered owner machine), or `{ condition: { ... } }` (fires once per subject edge on the workspace owner). `cron`, `every_minutes` and `deliveries_landed` take an optional `when` CEL guard over workspace state; `cron` and `every_minutes` also take `guard_miss` (`wait`, the default, or `skip`). Required.

template.description: Task template: `{ title, description?, acceptance_criteria?, task_type?, tags?, required_tools?, priority?, complexity?, crew?, status? }`. `complexity` is an assessed low/medium/hard/xhard value copied to every minted task; omission retains legacy unassessed minting. `required_tools` is an exact canonical-name list copied to every minted task. Provider-neutral — no turn knobs. Required.

workspace.description: Workspace selector for the authoritative server: a registered workspace name, a logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or an absolute path registered on that server. Optional in this session, which is already bound to a workspace — by `orbit mcp serve --workspace` at launch or `_meta.orbit.workspace` at initialize. Pass it to address a different registered workspace; never inferred from the server process cwd.

view.description: bounded: bounded metadata, explicit workspace, pagination and display truncation. Omit for the existing full-record response.

name: orbit_auto_task_mint
description: Mint one task now from an auto-task definition. Unconditional: the schedule, dedupe policy, and enabled flag are ignored, and the scheduler's own cursor is left untouched.

workspace.description: Explicit workspace for acknowledged mint

acknowledge_unconditional.description: True acknowledges unconditional creation; requires operator authority

name: orbit_auto_task_update
description: Update an existing auto-task definition (present fields only), including enabling or disabling it.

waive_batch.description: Explicit settled-batch waiver: { batch_id, reason }. Cannot be combined with definition edits; advances no coverage.

schedule.description: New schedule object: `{ cron: string }` `{ every_minutes: number }`, `{ deliveries_landed: { branch, threshold, max_wait_minutes, coverage, owner_machine?, max_items?, retries? } }` (owner_machine defaults to this workspace's registered owner machine) (coverage: landed_code_review_v1), or `{ condition: { ... } }` (fires once per subject edge on the workspace owner). `cron`, `every_minutes` and `deliveries_landed` take an optional `when` CEL guard over workspace state; `cron` and `every_minutes` also take `guard_miss` (`wait`, the default, or `skip`).

template.description: Replacement task template object, including optional assessed `complexity` (low/medium/hard/xhard) and exact canonical `required_tools` copied to minted tasks.

enabled.description: Enable (`true`) or disable (`false`) the definition. Disabling is the kill-switch, not a delete.

expected_enabled.description: Observed enabled state, checked atomically with the `enabled` change; the change is refused when the definition no longer matches. Requires operator authority and `workspace`, and accepts no other edits.

workspace.description: Explicit workspace, required with `expected_enabled`

name: orbit_automation_explain
description: Explain one routine's `trigger.condition` or auto-task's `schedule.condition` over the workspace's live state, without writing anything: its scope, the store prefilter and literal cross-reads, the ownership verdict, the current matches (up to 20, each with its arm state and remaining hold) and closest misses (up to 20; subjects failing exactly one top-level clause), and for one subject the tree of top-level && and || clauses with each clause's value and the operand values it read. Values that cannot be read evaluate as unknown, never false. `tracking` is the durable state: arm states and holds, any stall, the last pass and skip, recent fires with their upstream chain, and `self`. With `job:<name>` it reports that job's auto-task steps as checked at load instead: the outer `expire_when` bound, whether admission pins a source revision, and for each step its target auto-task (resolved, missing or unreadable, with its file digest, enabled state and own condition guard), `when`, `wait_until`, `expire_when`, `reuse_when`, `require_result` and the earlier steps it reads. Explain evaluates no wait and mints nothing; an enabled job's executions run detached and park while a step waits.

definition.description: The routine or auto-task carrying the condition: its name, or `routine:<name>` / `auto-task:<name>` when a routine and an auto-task share the name. `job:<name>` explains that job's auto-task steps instead.

subject.description: The subject whose clause tree to show: a task ID for a task-scope condition, `workspace` for a workspace-scope one. Default: the first match, else the first closest miss, else the first subject evaluated.

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (codex, claude, gemini, grok, or muse); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

name: orbit_friction_add
description: Append a friction report

body.description: Markdown body describing what happened and why it caused friction

title.description: One-line handle identifying the problem, at most 120 characters. This is what lists and searches show, so name the surface and the failure. Derived from the body's opening line when omitted

tags.description: Friction taxonomy tags as a string or array. Vocabulary: `automation` — Scheduler, auto-task, or delivery-automation friction; `build` — make/fmt/lint friction; `docs` — Stale or missing CLAUDE.md or design docs; `history-diverged` — A rewritten branch history orphaned recorded automation state; `lifecycle` — Task lifecycle confusion or transition issues; `naming` — Naming drift or duplicated sources of truth; `other` — Fallback; `policy` — fsProfile or sandboxing surprises; `skill-guidance` — Misleading or incorrect skill instructions; `tooling` — Tool, CLI, or MCP failures. Accepted aliases: ci → build, test → build, tests → build, testing → build, cli → tooling, mcp → tooling, tool → tooling, auto-task → automation, auto-tasks → automation, scheduler → automation, routine → automation, skill → skill-guidance, prompt → skill-guidance.

during_task.description: Optional task ID being worked on when friction occurred; an ID that names no task is refused

model.description: Required agent family for attribution (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`)

workspace.description: Workspace selector for the authoritative server: a registered workspace name, a logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or an absolute path registered on that server. Optional in this session, which is already bound to a workspace — by `orbit mcp serve --workspace` at launch or `_meta.orbit.workspace` at initialize. Pass it to address a different registered workspace; never inferred from the server process cwd.

name: orbit_friction_update
description: Update triage metadata for a friction record. A non-empty `rehome_to` moves the record into that registered workspace after the other edits apply: the owning workspace gets a copy with the original title, reporter, creation time, task, status, and body under a new ID (returned as `rehomed_as`), and this record is resolved with a pointer to it. Set `move` to false to only record the `rehome_to` disposition

status.description: Optional status: open, triaged, or resolved

tags.description: Friction taxonomy tags as a string or array. Vocabulary: `automation` — Scheduler, auto-task, or delivery-automation friction; `build` — make/fmt/lint friction; `docs` — Stale or missing CLAUDE.md or design docs; `history-diverged` — A rewritten branch history orphaned recorded automation state; `lifecycle` — Task lifecycle confusion or transition issues; `naming` — Naming drift or duplicated sources of truth; `other` — Fallback; `policy` — fsProfile or sandboxing surprises; `skill-guidance` — Misleading or incorrect skill instructions; `tooling` — Tool, CLI, or MCP failures. Accepted aliases: ci → build, test → build, tests → build, testing → build, cli → tooling, mcp → tooling, tool → tooling, auto-task → automation, auto-tasks → automation, scheduler → automation, routine → automation, skill → skill-guidance, prompt → skill-guidance.

rehome_to.description: Optional registered workspace that owns a friction recorded in the wrong one; moves the record there unless `move` is false. An empty string clears a recorded disposition

move.description: With `rehome_to`: false records the `rehome_required` disposition without moving, for a workspace that is not registered here; defaults to true

title.description: Optional replacement one-line title, at most 120 characters; an empty string restores derivation from the body

workspace.description: Workspace selector for the authoritative server: a registered workspace name, a logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or an absolute path registered on that server. Optional in this session, which is already bound to a workspace — by `orbit mcp serve --workspace` at launch or `_meta.orbit.workspace` at initialize. Pass it to address a different registered workspace; never inferred from the server process cwd.

name: orbit_search
description: Search tasks and frictions using lexical matching. With `kind: friction` and no `query`, list friction records instead: every status unless a `friction:` status narrows it, filtered by `tag`, ordered by creation time then ID, each hit carrying the full `record`; a note reports a listing cut at `limit`.

query.description: Tasks match non-adjacent terms: full matches first, then partial matches by term count and BM25. Frictions match a case-insensitive substring. Optional with `kind: friction`, where omitting it lists frictions.

kind.description: Corpus kind: task, friction, or all. Default: all.

limit.description: Maximum number of results, at most 1000. Default: 10, or 1000 for a friction listing.

tag.description: AND-filter by tag. Repeat or pass an array. Applies to task and friction.

all.description: Include every status for the queried kind. Task defaults to proposed/backlog/in-progress/review/blocked; all adds done/rejected/archived/someday. Friction query defaults to open; all adds triaged/resolved.

status.description: Explicit per-kind status override using kind:value tokens, such as task:open or friction:open. task:open covers proposed/backlog/in-progress/review/blocked. Overrides `all` for the named kind.

workspaces.description: Federated scope: registered workspace names, `ws_*` IDs, or absolute checkout paths to search together. Hits carry workspace attribution. Omit to search only the bound workspace.

all_workspaces.description: Search every active workspace registered on the answering machine. Overrides `workspaces`. Not available inside an Orbit-managed run.

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (codex, claude, gemini, grok, or muse); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

name: orbit_task_add
description: Create an Orbit task and return the created task JSON

workspace.description: Workspace selector: a registered workspace name, a logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or an absolute path to a local checkout (a linked Git worktree resolves to its registered checkout). Falls back to the MCP session's `_meta.orbit.workspace` when omitted; never inferred from process cwd.

acceptance_criteria.description: Optional acceptance criteria as a string or array of strings

tags.description: Optional tags as a string or array of strings. `os:linux`, `os:macos` or `os:windows` limits which host OS may run the task (several: any one of them); any other `os:` value is rejected

required_tools.description: Optional exact canonical tool names the task adds to its agent activity baseline, as a string or array of strings

granted_tools.description: Optional exact canonical tool names an operator grants the implementing activity despite its deny list, as a string or array of strings. Requires operator authority: any other caller supplying it is refused, never stripped. Stored and shown. Only the implementing activity (`agent_implement`) reads a grant: it lifts that tool's deny entry only for a read/repeat-safe tool, and a mutating tool stays denied

requires_labels.description: Optional capability labels a host must carry, all of them, to run the task, as a string or array of strings. A host carries its `machine.labels` plus its OS (`linux`, `macos` or `windows`). Refused when no registered serving host carries them together with the task's `os:` tags

not_before.description: Optional scheduled start: an RFC 3339 instant with an offset, such as `2026-11-06T09:00:00Z`, stored in UTC. No dispatcher starts the task from the backlog before it; the hold lifts by itself on the first admission pass after it. A malformed time is refused

context_files.description: Optional task context selectors as a comma-separated string or array of strings. Add entries ONLY for existing files, directories, or symbols expected to be modified or deleted by the task. Do not add background-reading entries or files referenced only for context. Prefer canonical selectors: `file:`, `dir:`, or `symbol:path#name:kind`. Legacy raw paths are accepted and upgraded automatically. Existence checks verify the filesystem anchor only; a `symbol:` name and kind are not looked up.

allow_missing_context.description: Optional. Set true to accept `context_files` selectors whose target does not exist yet, for work that creates the file. Each such selector is recorded on the task as durable creation intent for that exact selector, which later writes and task preparation honor. Syntax, workspace containment and file/directory kind are still checked. Missing selectors are rejected by default.

complexity.description: Required for ordinary creation; omit for guarded request_id creation. Task complexity level (low, medium, hard, or xhard). Accepted aliases: easy, small, or trivial → low; large or big → hard

relations.description: Optional typed task relations as an array of {type, target} objects. A `regression_from` relation may add `regression: {nature, escape, severity, severity_source?, sites?}`: nature is broke_existing, defect_in_new, incomplete, merge_reintroduced, contract_drift or unclassified; escape is no_test, test_not_selected, platform_only, review_missed, spec_ambiguous, nondeterministic or unclassified; severity is required and is critical (data loss, a security hole, every drain halted, silently wrong results), high (a core workflow broken with no workaround), medium (a feature broken in a real path, with a workaround), low (an edge case or misleading message) or nit (wording, doc drift, cosmetic); severity_source is filer (the default), operator or backfill; optional `sites` lists up to 8 `symbol:` or `file:` selectors of where the defect lives, or a `dir:` selector when no narrower site can be named

crew.description: Optional named crew to use when running this task; omitted, one is drawn from the complexity pool or the configured default

orchestrator.description: Optional named crew responsible for orchestration attribution; does not select execution. Defaults to the MCP session's `orbit mcp serve --orchestrator` crew when omitted

orchestrator_model.description: Optional model the orchestrator runs, only when it differs from the `orchestrator` crew's configured model. Omitted, the task records that crew's configured model at creation. Requires an orchestrator, is set once at creation and never updated. Unrelated to `model`, which labels the writer

origin.description: Optional reason the task was filed: `operator_request` when a human asked for the work, `orchestrator_initiative` when the orchestrator decided on its own, `automation` for a system filer. Omitted, it stays unset, except that system filers and sweep findings record `automation`.

fields.description: Optional response field names as a string or array. Defaults omit `comments` and `history`; request them explicitly. Catalogue and projection semantics: installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

field.description: Compatibility alias for a single response field projection, such as `field: "history"`.

request_id.description: Optional retry-safe proposed creation. Requires explicit workspace and acceptance_criteria; accepts only title, description, acceptance_criteria, priority and crew. Reuse the identity with identical input to reconcile a lost reply. Returns a versioned snapshot.

model.description: Preferred provenance field: the agent family (codex, claude, gemini, grok, or muse) or a full model string such as `claude-opus-5-5`. `created_by` records the family; a full model string is also recorded once as `created_by_model`. A value that names no known family is refused.

name: orbit_task_artifact_get
description: Read one stored task artifact by owning task ID and artifact path. Returns `media_type`, `size`, and the bytes: UTF-8 text as `content`, and everything else as base64 in `content_base64`. Supported raster images (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP) whose bytes match their declared type are additionally returned as a viewable image on transports that carry image content, so a multimodal client can inspect a stored visual reference directly. SVG, HTML, and any payload whose bytes contradict its media type are returned as opaque base64 and are never rendered. List available artifacts first with `orbit_task_show` and `field: "artifacts"`; payloads are fetched only through this call. Reads are bounded to 1048576 bytes.

id.description: Globally unique task ID that owns the artifact.

path.description: Artifact path relative to the task artifacts directory, exactly as it appears in `orbit_task_show` with `field: "artifacts"`. Absolute paths and `..` are rejected.

agent.description: Deprecated compatibility field. Prefer `model` with the agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`).

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

workspace.description: Optional explicit workspace filter. `id` is resolved globally by default; when supplied, a registered workspace name, logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or absolute local checkout path is fail-closed — a valid workspace that does not own the task returns not-found.

name: orbit_task_artifact_put
description: Store a file (any content, up to 1 MiB) as a task artifact. Sources must stay inside the workspace after symlink resolution; write evidence under `.orbit/tmp/`. Artifact paths beginning with `review-` in any ASCII case are reserved for the review gate's system writer; the only agent-writable exception is the schema-checked `review-report.json`. Name ordinary supporting evidence with a nonreserved name (for example `examination-checks.json`). See the assigned task's evidence template for automation coverage and review report contracts.

source_path.description: Source file to store as a task artifact. Resolved against the caller cwd, not the checkout root, so a file that exists only at the checkout root is refused with the absolute path to pass. Then confined to the workspace checkout after symlink resolution. Absolute paths and symlinks that escape the workspace are rejected. Write evidence under `.orbit/tmp/` (`$ORBIT_SCRATCH_DIR`); sources under `/tmp` are outside the workspace and are refused.

path.description: Artifact path relative to the task artifacts directory. Defaults to the source file name. Paths beginning with `review-` in any ASCII case are reserved for the review gate's system writer; the only agent-writable exception is the schema-checked `review-report.json`. Rename ordinary supporting evidence to a nonreserved name (for example `examination-checks.json`).

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (codex, claude, gemini, grok, or muse); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

workspace.description: Workspace selector for the authoritative server: a registered workspace name, a logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or an absolute path registered on that server. Optional in this session, which is already bound to a workspace — by `orbit mcp serve --workspace` at launch or `_meta.orbit.workspace` at initialize. Pass it to address a different registered workspace. An id whose prefix belongs to another registered host is refused with `task_prefix_remote`, naming that host; this server does not relay. Never inferred from the server process cwd.

name: orbit_task_block_triage
description: Triage blocked tasks whose final recovery escalated, or that the backstop never decides. `candidates` lists those awaiting triage; `propose` records options and a recommendation, `report` records a human action, and `requeue` returns the task to the backlog within the requeue bound shared with final recovery. Never completes, rejects or archives a task. With `subject` `pilot_warning`, the same actions triage proposed tasks held by a task-pilot warning instead, and `requeue` is refused. A refused requeue leaves the task blocked. A decision on a task a live triage run holds needs that run's inspection proof. Policy detail, the requeue bound, the pilot-warning marker and the proof recipe: the orbit skill's references/tool-surface.md, section `Blocked-task triage`.

workspace.description: Workspace selector from discovery. Omitted, a bound session uses its workspace and an unbound one resolves the task id through this host's task registry

subject.description: what is triaged: block (default), a blocked task's block episode; pilot_warning, a proposed task's pilot warning hold

id.description: requeue, propose, report: the blocked or pilot-held task

blocker.description: block requeue, propose, report: the escalation reason, quoted in the comment; pilot_warning quotes the holding findings itself and refuses it

reason.description: requeue: the repair applied and why the task can run again; report: the specific action only a human can take

options.description: propose: two or three {summary, consequences, target, replacement} objects; target is `acceptance_criteria` or `description`, and replacement is that field's complete new value (one criterion per line), which an operator's answer applies; without a target the option cannot be applied

recommended.description: propose: 1-based index of the recommended option

source_revision.description: inspection proof: the pinned commit id the caller inspected, or null in a non-Git workspace; supply with observed_revision and observed_tree

observed_revision.description: inspection proof: `git rev-parse HEAD` in the inspection checkout

observed_tree.description: inspection proof: `git rev-parse 'HEAD^{tree}'` in the inspection checkout

agent.description: Deprecated compatibility field. Prefer `model` with the agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`).

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

name: orbit_task_eligible
description: List backlog and proposed tasks that can be picked up now without colliding with work in flight, as {tasks, total, truncated[, conflicting]}. A task is eligible when its context-file lock surface overlaps no in-progress or review task's surface, decided by the same lock code automatic dispatch uses. No other gate applies: dependencies, complexity, groups, crew and overlap between candidates are not checked. Read-only.

status.description: Candidate statuses: `backlog`, `proposed`, or both (the default). Pass a comma-separated string or an array.

path.description: Keep only candidates whose `context_files` selectors apply to this path, matched as `orbit_task_list` matches `path`.

limit.description: Maximum eligible tasks to return (default 50). Must be at least 1.

explain.description: When true, also return `conflicting`: every held-back candidate with the overlapping selector and the in-progress or review task holding it.

agent.description: Deprecated compatibility field. Prefer `model` with the agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`).

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

workspace.description: Workspace selector for the authoritative server: a registered workspace name, a logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or an absolute path registered on that server. Pass it to address a different registered workspace; never inferred from the server process cwd.

name: orbit_task_list
description: List Orbit tasks in a {tasks, total, truncated} envelope (default limit 50). With no status filter, non-terminal tasks come first and terminal tasks follow, each newest first; an explicit status filter is newest first. `total` counts all matching tasks and `truncated` reports whether the limit omitted tasks. Each task is a compact row (see `fields`); pass `fields` to add long-text fields such as description or plan. Optional filters: status, parent, type, origin, tag, dependency readiness, path, runs_on, not_before_from, not_before_until (inclusive RFC 3339 bounds; unscheduled tasks do not match). scheduled:true lists future schedules soonest first, including proposed tasks. Default rows carry not_before (null when unset). os_requirement is derived from OS tags intersected with the stored crew executor host_os, with source and unresolved/conflict states.

status.description: Optional task status filter. Pass a comma-separated string or an array of status names.

parent_id.description: Optional parent task ID to list subtasks for

scheduled.description: Keep only future not_before schedules, soonest first, including proposed tasks. Other filters still apply.

not_before_from.description: Inclusive lower not_before bound (RFC 3339 with an offset). Unscheduled tasks do not match.

not_before_until.description: Inclusive upper not_before bound (RFC 3339 with an offset). Unscheduled tasks do not match.

origin.description: Optional task origin filter: operator_request, orchestrator_initiative or automation. Tasks without a recorded origin never match.

tag.description: Filter by tag. Repeat or pass an array for AND semantics.

runs_on.description: Filter by effective host OS: linux, macos or windows. Intersects OS tags with the stored crew executor. Unrestricted tasks match; unresolved crews and conflicts do not.

ready.description: When true, keep only tasks whose dependencies are satisfied

path.description: Filter to tasks whose `context_files` selectors apply to this path. Supports file:, dir:, symbol:, and bare path selectors; bidirectional containment.

limit.description: Maximum number of tasks to return (default 50). With no status filter, non-terminal tasks come first and terminal tasks follow, each newest first. Must be at least 1.

fields.description: Optional per-task field projection as a string or array, using the field names `orbit_task_show` accepts (for example `id`, `title`, `status`). When set, each listed task is an object holding only those fields. Omit it for compact rows (id, title, status, priority, type, dependencies, resolved_dependencies, implemented_by, not_before, created_at, updated_at, workspace), the same rows `orbit tool run orbit.task.list` returns. For long-text fields such as description, acceptance_criteria, plan or execution_summary, name them here, or fetch one task with `orbit_task_show`.

view.description: bounded: bounded metadata, pagination and display truncation. It always needs an explicit `workspace` selector copied from `orbit_workspace_list`, even in a workspace-bound session; without one the call is refused. Omit for the default response.

external_ref.description: Optional exact external reference filter in `system:id` form

has_ref.description: Optional external reference system filter: keep tasks with any reference in this system

agent.description: Deprecated compatibility field. Prefer `model` with the agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`).

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

Optional in this session, which is already bound to a workspace — by `orbit mcp serve --workspace` at launch or `_meta.orbit.workspace` at initialize. Pass it to address a different registered workspace; never inferred from the server process cwd.

name: orbit_task_show
description: Fetch a task as JSON by globally unique `id`; optional `workspace` is a fail-closed filter. Use `fields` (alias `field`) for projections, or `field: "delivery"` for bounded commit/landing evidence. Projection, routing and delivery details: installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

id.description: Globally unique task ID. Resolved through the host task registry by default; a workspace argument is not required.

snapshot.description: True returns a bounded versioned snapshot with opaque revision and available actions. Requires explicit workspace; snapshot grants no authority and cannot combine with field projections.

agent.description: Deprecated compatibility field. Prefer `model` with the agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`).

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (`codex`, `claude`, `gemini`, `grok`, or `muse`); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

fields.description: Optional field names as a string or array; returns only those fields. `delivery` must be selected alone. Catalogue and response semantics: installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

field.description: Compatibility alias for a single field projection. Example: `field: "artifacts"`.

run_id.description: With `field: "delivery"` only: the delivery run to report. Omitted, the newest task-delivery run submitted with this task is used.

workspace.description: Optional explicit workspace filter. `id` is resolved globally by default; do not pass cwd, MCP session/initialize metadata, or a linked-worktree runtime identity (for example `orbit-5c61b3`). When supplied, a registered workspace name, logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or absolute local checkout path is fail-closed: a valid workspace that does not own the task returns not-found, and an unknown selector is rejected by name.

view.description: bounded: bounded metadata, pagination and display truncation. It always needs an explicit `workspace` selector copied from `orbit_workspace_list`, even in a workspace-bound session; without one the call is refused. Omit for the default response.

name: orbit_task_update
description: Update an Orbit task and return the fresh task JSON. Field edits may accompany a status change, except `status: backlog` on a proposed task (approval), which accepts only `note` and `comment`. Starting with `status: in-progress` from a pickup state may include field edits on the same write.

acceptance_criteria.description: New acceptance criteria as an array of strings or a single string

dependencies.description: Replacement dependency task IDs as a string or array of strings

relations.description: Replacement typed task relations as an array of {type, target} objects. A `regression_from` relation may add `regression: {nature, escape, severity, severity_source?, sites?}`: nature is broke_existing, defect_in_new, incomplete, merge_reintroduced, contract_drift or unclassified; escape is no_test, test_not_selected, platform_only, review_missed, spec_ambiguous, nondeterministic or unclassified; severity is critical (data loss, a security hole, every drain halted, silently wrong results), high (a core workflow broken with no workaround), medium (a feature broken in a real path, with a workaround), low (an edge case or misleading message) or nit (wording, doc drift, cosmetic), required on a link the task does not hold yet, while a held link re-sent without one keeps its recorded severity and source; severity_source is filer (the default), operator or backfill, and reads back as verified once finding verification rates the link or default for a link stored without a severity; optional `sites` lists up to 8 `symbol:` or `file:` selectors of where the defect lives, or a `dir:` selector when no narrower site can be named

tags.description: Replacement task tags as a string or array of strings. `os:linux`, `os:macos` or `os:windows` limits which host OS may run the task from its next admission; any other `os:` value is rejected

granted_tools.description: Replacement operator-granted tool names, as a string or array of strings; an empty array clears the grant. Requires operator authority: any other caller supplying it is refused, never stripped. Accepted only while the task is proposed, backlog or someday with no live run or claim; a grant is frozen once an attempt is dispatched and changes only for a new attempt. Stored and shown. Only the implementing activity (`agent_implement`) reads a grant: it lifts that tool's deny entry only for a read/repeat-safe tool, and a mutating tool stays denied

requires_labels.description: Replacement capability labels a host must carry, all of them, to run the task from its next admission, as a string or array of strings; an empty array clears it. A host carries its `machine.labels` plus its OS. Refused when no registered serving host carries them together with the task's `os:` tags

not_before.description: Replacement scheduled start: an RFC 3339 instant with an offset, such as `2026-11-06T09:00:00Z`, stored in UTC; an empty string clears it (null, like any omitted field, leaves it unchanged). No dispatcher starts a backlog task before it, and the hold lifts by itself on the first admission pass after it. A malformed time is refused

allow_drop_system_tags.description: Optional. Set true to permit replacing `tags` with a list that drops a system identity tag (`ci-failure:*`). Missing or false rejects the tag drop.

plan.description: Replacement task plan text (empty string clears). May be supplied on the same write that transitions to in-progress when a plan is required.

status.description: New task status. `backlog` on a proposed task is the approval transition and cannot be combined with field edits (only `note` and `comment`). `in-progress` from a pickup state is the start transition and may include field edits on the same write; from any other status that start is refused whether or not extra fields are present. Other status changes are ordinary governed updates and may include field edits.

note.description: Annotation stored on this status transition's history entry; use `comment` for free-form discussion

priority.description: New dispatch priority (low, medium, high, or critical)

complexity.description: Optional task complexity level (low, medium, hard, or xhard). Accepted aliases: easy, small, or trivial → low; large or big → hard

source_task_id.description: For bug tasks: originating task ID that introduced the defect (empty string clears)

planned_by.description: Explicit planning attribution label (empty string clears)

implemented_by.description: Explicit implementation attribution label (empty string clears)

pr_status.description: PR review status (e.g. approve, request-changes; empty string clears)

job_run_id.description: Job run ID to associate with the task (empty string clears)

crew.description: Named crew to use when running this task (empty string draws a fresh one)

orchestrator.description: Named crew responsible for orchestration attribution (empty string clears; mutable only before execution)

origin.description: Replacement reason the task was filed: operator_request, orchestrator_initiative or automation. Corrects a recorded origin; it cannot be cleared.

context_files.description: Replaces the whole selector list; omit both context fields to preserve it. To extend, read `context_files` and send the deduplicated union of all existing and new selectors. Policy and clear/create cases: installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

allow_missing_context.description: Accept missing targets for files this task creates, recording durable creation intent per selector. Missing targets are rejected by default. Persistence and validation rules: installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

context.description: Legacy string alias for `context_files`, which takes precedence. Replaces the whole list; to extend, read and send the union of all existing and new selectors. Omit both to preserve. Policy: installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

fields.description: Optional response field names as a string or array. Defaults omit `comments` and `history`; request them explicitly. Catalogue and projection semantics: installed Orbit skill `references/task-fields.md`.

field.description: Compatibility alias for a single response field projection, such as `field: "history"`.

request_id.description: Optional retry-safe guarded write identity. Requires explicit workspace and expected_revision. Reuse identical input to reconcile a lost reply; returns a fresh versioned snapshot.

expected_revision.description: Observed revision from task.show snapshot:true. Guarded mode accepts field edits, a comment, or a verdict separately.

complete.description: Guarded review only: explicitly complete an accepted review with existing trusted operator authority. Default false; never merges, publishes or dispatches.

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (codex, claude, gemini, grok, or muse); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

workspace.description: Workspace selector for the authoritative server: a registered workspace name, a logical workspace ID (`ws_*`), or an absolute path registered on that server. Optional in this session, which is already bound to a workspace — by `orbit mcp serve --workspace` at launch or `_meta.orbit.workspace` at initialize. Pass it to address a different registered workspace. An id whose prefix belongs to another registered host is refused with `task_prefix_remote`, naming that host; this server does not relay. Never inferred from the server process cwd.

name: orbit_visual_capture
description: Render the current working tree (uncommitted changes included) for each of a task's `mocks/` artifacts and write, per mock, `mock.png`, `capture.png` and `side-by-side.png` plus one `rules.json` with the workspace's UI rule results for those captures, under the output directory. Each mock name gives the view, state, theme and width, resolved against the view manifests configured in `visual_review.manifests`, whose fixture serves the app. This is the implementer's self-check: it attaches nothing and records nothing on the task, and its output is not evidence of record. Needs a verified browser kit on the host and a configured manifest; without either it fails naming what is missing. A mock whose view never renders is reported per mock as `render_timeout`, and one whose app's setup fails as `setup_failed`.

id.description: Task ID whose `mocks/` artifacts name the views to capture.

mock.description: Capture only this one mock artifact (its full `mocks/…` path) instead of every mock of the task.

out.description: Directory the captures are written under, one subdirectory per mock. Defaults to `.orbit/tmp/visual/<task-id>` in the checkout.

model.description: Preferred provenance field. Pass the canonical agent family (codex, claude, gemini, grok, or muse); full model strings are accepted and auto-normalized.

Optional in this session, which is already bound to a workspace — by `orbit mcp serve --workspace` at launch or `_meta.orbit.workspace` at initialize. Pass it to address a different registered workspace. An id whose prefix belongs to another registered host is refused with `task_prefix_remote`, naming that host; this server does not relay. name: orbit_workspace_list
description: List active workspaces with a checkout registered on this machine, optionally with each one's configured crews.

include.description: Optional extra detail per workspace row. `crews` adds the workspace's effective configured crews and default crew as `crews`, read on the machine that holds the checkout, or `crews_error` when its configuration cannot be read.
